gloss: name and reality; reputation and substance

definitions.gloss: name and reality; both in name and in fact
definitions.explanation: The relationship between what something is called or reputed to be and what it actually is. Formed from {名|めい} (name) and {実|じつ} (reality, substance). Almost always used in the set phrase {名実|めいじつ}ともに.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{名実|めいじつ}ともにリーダーだ。
examples.english: He is a leader both in name and in fact.

examples.japanese: この{店|みせ}は{名実|めいじつ}ともに{地域|ちいき}{一番|いちばん}だ。
examples.english: This shop is number one in the area, both in reputation and in reality.

examples.japanese: {優勝|ゆうしょう}して、{名実|めいじつ}ともに{日本一|にほんいち}のチームになった。
examples.english: By winning the championship, they became the best team in Japan in both name and substance.

notes:
Nearly always appears in the fixed adverbial phrase {名実|めいじつ}ともに (both in name and in reality), used to stress that a title or reputation is fully matched by the facts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {名実|めいじつ}ともに: both in name and in fact
- {名実|めいじつ}{相伴|あいともな}う: for name and substance to go together

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {有名無実|ゆうめいむじつ}: nominal; in name only — the opposite situation, where reputation is not backed by reality.
- {実質|じっしつ}: substance; essence — focuses on the actual content rather than the name.
